title: MCP Tools for Todo Task Management
description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool definitions for AI-powered task management. These tools enable an AI agent to perform CRUD operations on todo tasks through a stateless, tool-driven architecture.

tools.name: add_task
tools.description: Add a new task to the user's todo list. Use this when the user wants to create a new task, add something to their list, or remember to do something.

title.description: The title or name of the task. Should be concise and descriptive.

description.description: Optional detailed description or notes about the task.
examples: Need milk, eggs, bread, and coffee
Include Q4 sales figures and projections for Q1

user_id.description: The ID of the user who owns this task. Must be provided by the backend.

success.description: Whether the task was created successfully

error.description: Error message if success is false

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Retrieve all tasks for the user. Use this when the user wants to see their tasks, check what's on their list, or review their todos. Can optionally filter by completion status.

user_id.description: The ID of the user whose tasks to retrieve. Must be provided by the backend.

completed.description: Optional filter: true for completed tasks only, false for pending tasks only, omit for all tasks

tasks.description: List of tasks matching the criteria

error.description: Error message if success is false

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Update an existing task's title, description, or completion status. Use this when the user wants to modify a task, change its details, or mark it as complete/incomplete.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to update

user_id.description: The ID of the user who owns this task. Must be provided by the backend for authorization.

examples: Get milk, eggs, and whole grain bread from Whole Foods

success.description: Whether the task was updated successfully

error.description: Error message if success is false (e.g., 'Task not found', 'Access denied')

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Mark a task as completed. Use this when the user indicates they have finished a task, completed something, or are done with a todo item. This is a convenience wrapper around update_task.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to mark as completed

user_id.description: The ID of the user who owns this task. Must be provided by the backend for authorization.

success.description: Whether the task was marked as completed successfully

error.description: Error message if success is false

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Permanently delete a task from the user's list. Use this when the user wants to remove a task, delete something from their list, or get rid of a todo item. This action cannot be undone.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to delete

user_id.description: The ID of the user who owns this task. Must be provided by the backend for authorization.

success.description: Whether the task was deleted successfully

error.description: Error message if success is false

metadata.author: Todo Application Team
notes: All tools require user_id for authorization
Tools enforce user ownership - users can only access their own tasks
Tools return structured responses with success flag and optional error message
Task IDs are UUIDs generated by the backend
All tools are stateless and idempotent where applicable

intent_mapping.create: Use add_task when user wants to create, add, or remember something
intent_mapping.read: Use list_tasks when user wants to see, view, or check their tasks
intent_mapping.update: Use update_task when user wants to modify, change, or edit task details
intent_mapping.complete: Use complete_task when user indicates they finished or completed a task
intent_mapping.delete: Use delete_task when user wants to remove, delete, or get rid of a task

error_handling.task_not_found: Inform user the task doesn't exist and offer to list their tasks
error_handling.access_denied: Inform user they don't have permission (should not happen in normal flow)
error_handling.validation_error: Explain what was invalid and ask for clarification
error_handling.service_error: Apologize and suggest trying again or contacting support

conversational_patterns.ambiguous_reference: If user says 'complete the task' but multiple tasks exist, ask which one
conversational_patterns.confirmation: After successful operations, confirm what was done with task details
conversational_patterns.friendly_tone: Use natural, conversational language in responses
